value.body: Public-sector banks recruit clerks and probationary officers (POs) through national exams. IBPS (Institute of Banking Personnel Selection) runs common exams for most public-sector banks and for Regional Rural Banks, while the State Bank of India (SBI) runs its own. Clerks handle customer and branch operations; POs start as junior managers.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A graduate degree in any discipline is required, so after Class 12 students complete a degree first, and many start preparing during it. Age limits are typically 20–28 for clerk and 20–30 for PO, with category relaxations — the notification for each cycle is the reference. Selection runs through an online preliminary exam and a main exam, plus an interview for PO posts.

value.title: At a glance
items: Exams test reasoning, quantitative aptitude and English, with banking and general awareness in the mains.
PO postings can be anywhere in India; clerk recruitment is state-wise and often requires the local language.
Vacancy numbers change every year and are often revised after the notification.
IBPS RRB exams are a separate entry, for Officer Scale-I and Office Assistant posts in Regional Rural Banks.
